unmapped_findings: Hydrogen embrittlement in Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C was mainly due to two distinct phenomena: (1) cracking at grain boundary triple junctions; (2) gradual formation of chains of microvoids on grain boundaries under pronounced planar slip localization, leading to void coalescence and intergranular cracking along the affected grain boundaries [b0105].
The intense slip localization mechanism was suggested to be linked to the presence of κ-carbides in this steel [b0105].

κ-carbides can act as beneficial hydrogen trapping sites (estimated activation energy 76–80 kJ/mol) that might render hydrogen immobile, while the associated hydrogen-assisted planar slip acts in the opposite direction by promoting grain-boundary void formation [b0106][b0107].
Hydrogen charging produced only a small loss of strength but a clearer loss of ductility in the Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C steel [figure_009].
